record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: What channel models and channel-estimation techniques are appropriate for RIS-aided near-field communication, where a large RIS violates the far-field planar-wave assumption and different RIS elements experience different angles and polarization conditions?

evidence.quote: Without the far-field assumption, the incident waves at different elements will have unequal angular directions and polarization.
Studying suitable channel models and associated estimation techniques for RIS-aided near field communication is a potential direction for future research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a wireless communication system aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS): a planar array of N passive reflecting elements whose individual reflection coefficients (phase shifts, and possibly amplitudes) can be configured to shape the propagation environment between a transmitter and a receiver. When the RIS aperture is large relative to the wavelength and to the distances involved, a receiver or transmitter may lie within the Rayleigh (near-field) region of the surface. In this regime the standard far-field planar-wave assumption fails: the wavefronts impinging on the surface are curved (spherical), and the angles of arrival/departure, path lengths, and polarization states differ from one RIS element to another, so that the channel cannot be described by a single steering vector parametrized by a single direction.

Formalize the following research problem:

(a) Propose a tractable mathematical channel model for the cascaded transmitter–RIS–receiver link in the near field of a large RIS, accounting for (i) element-dependent spherical wavefront curvature (e.g., per-element distance and angle), (ii) element-dependent polarization mismatch, and (iii) possible mutual coupling, such that the model reduces to the standard far-field planar-wave RIS channel model in the appropriate asymptotic limit.

(b) Design and analyze a channel-estimation algorithm that, given pilot symbols transmitted under a chosen sequence of RIS configurations, recovers the parameters of the proposed near-field channel model with provable guarantees (e.g., identifiability, sample/pilot complexity, mean-squared-error scaling) that exploit the structure (such as spherical-domain sparsity) of the near-field channel.

Determine appropriate models and estimators meeting (a) and (b), and characterize the trade-offs between pilot overhead, RIS size, near-field/far-field regime, and estimation accuracy.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent works (2022–2025) have proposed near-field RIS channel models based on spherical wavefronts and Fresnel approximations, and have developed estimation algorithms using compressive sensing in the polar/spherical domain, joint channel estimation and localization (NF-JCEL), and methods accounting for beam-squint in wideband XL-RIS systems. However, no single comprehensive model jointly handling spherical wavefronts, per-element polarization, mutual coupling, and wideband effects with provable estimation guarantees has been established; the area remains an active research direction.

status_evidence.title: Near-Field Channel Estimation for Extremely Large-Scale RIS-Aided Wideband mmWave Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Two-dimensional compressive sensing recovery of near-field channel parameters using spherical-domain sparsity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works partially address near-field RIS channel estimation via spherical-domain compressive sensing.

status_evidence.title: Joint Channel Estimation and Localization in the Near Field of RIS Enabled mmWave/subTHz Communications
status_evidence.snippet: NF-JCEL algorithm based on second-order Fresnel approximation of the near-field channel model.
status_evidence.claim: A near-field joint channel estimation and localization algorithm has been proposed.

status_evidence.title: A mini-review of signal processing techniques for RIS-assisted near field THz communication
status_evidence.snippet: Strategies for RIS-assisted near-field THz communication emphasize near-field channel estimation and beamforming.
status_evidence.claim: The topic is recognized as an open and active research direction.
